angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 146,514 km at 37.19 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 26.8860 +/- 0.0158 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 37.19 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2106 +/- 0.0061 solar radii from Ghachoui et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1680 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..31G/abstract): 146,514 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.1798 +/- 0.0044 solar masses from Ghachoui et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1680 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..31G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3225 +/- 99 K from Ghachoui et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1680 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..31G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ghachoui et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1680 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..31G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1680.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.046, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1680 (pscomppars): spectral type M4.5+/-0.5, from Ghachoui et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..31G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1680 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.04 dex, from Ghachoui et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..31G/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1680 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.36251, from Ghachoui et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..31G/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
